Shower coverage finally began to increase across the Marianas this
afternoon, with numerous heavy showers seen across Guam and scattered
showers elsewhere earlier this afternoon. POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) around on the low-end, around 30 percent, for the CNMI
and around 50 percent for Guam, which looks to be the rule through 
the rest of the night. Latest guidance tries to bring in numerous 
showers for the next couple of days for Guam, with very dry 
conditions across the CNMI. However, decided to maintain POPs at 30 
to 50 percent for Guam due to this increase in convection being 
linked to the development of a weak monsoon disturbance both 
southeast and southwest of Guam over the next few days. It appears 
that development, if it occurs, will be a bit farther away from Guam,
heading almost due north, keeping the heavier showers and higher 
POPs away from the Marianas. Therefore, Guam looks to maintain 
scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms for the next few days, 
with the CNMI seeing only isolated showers by Monday morning.

Marine...
For marine conditions, the winds looks to remain fairly benign for 
the Marianas through at least Wednesday. Then, seas could increase a
bit around midweek. Latest WaveWatch guidance is spread across a wide
range of sea heights. The ECMWF Wave model shows seas remaining at or
below 6 feet until Thursday, then only building to around 7 feet. The
GFS Wave, Global Wave and NWPS show seas reaching 10 to 12 feet
Thursday due to the GFS predicting the development of a tropical
disturbance on the east-northeast and southwest side of Guam. Since
the development is possible, yet not expected at this time, decided
to use a 75 percent ECMWF and 25 percent GFS Wave model blend,
bringing seas up to 9 feet. This will likely change over the next
couple of days as it becomes more evident whether these systems will
or will not develop. For winds, mostly light to gentle through
midweek, with winds becoming occasionally fresh after midweek due to
either the development of aforementioned disturbances or an
increasing monsoon surge.

Tropical Systems...
A monsoon depression, Invest 94W, is centered W of the far northern 
CNMI near 20N 134E, moving slowly west. 94W is now a subject of a 
Tropical Cyclone Formation Alert (TCFA), meaning development into a 
significant tropical cyclone is likely within the next 24 hours. 
Enhanced infrared satellite data currently shows a weak, disorganized
Low-Level Circulation Center (LLCC) with persistent, pulsing 
convection obscuring the center. The latest 925mb analysis shows an 
elongated LLCC with weak surrounding winds. Low vertical wind shear 
and favorable equatorward outflow combined with the favorable sea 
surface temperatures indicate conditions conducive for development. 

Eastern Micronesia...
Satellite imagery indicates numerous showers at Pohnpei, high-end 
scattered showers at Kosrae, and scattered showers at Majuro, with 
isolated thunderstorms near all three forecast points. Scatterometry 
indicates moderate to fresh southwesterlies across much of Pohnpei 
and Kosrae, and gentle to moderate southwesterlies at Majuro. 
Altimetry and buoy data indicates combined seas of 5 to 7 ft near 
Pohnpei and Kosrae, and 4 to 6 ft at Majuro.

A monsoon surge aided by a broad circulation well to the northwest is
producing widespread convection with numerous showers and locally 
heavy rainfall over Pohnpei. Model guidance indicates this pattern 
continuing through Monday night, so a headline with additional 
wording was included in the forecast without the need for a Special 
Weather Statement as flooding and mudslides are not a concern as of
now. Should conditions last longer or intensify more than previously
anticipated, an SPS may need to be issued. This situation will
continue to be monitored.

As for Kosrae, the heaviest convection and strongest winds should 
remain to the north, but numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms 
are still expected at least through Monday afternoon. Finally, Majuro
will remain within diffusive flow and near a col to the northeast, 
so light winds, scattered showers, and isolated thunderstorms are 
possible through Monday night. Afterwards, the active weather 
pattern may settle down through the rest of the week for the entire 
region.

A brief pulse in the westerly swell is expected at Pohnpei, 
temporarily increasing combined seas in their coastal waters as well
as surf heights along west-facing reefs. As of now, there is little 
concern for hazardous seas to small craft nor hazardous surf because
the swell pulse is not expected to last beyond Monday night. 
However, a headline was included for the elevated surf along west- 
facing reefs, so beachgoers should remain vigilant in or near the 
waters as the risk of rip currents will be moderate. As for Kosrae 
and Majuro, benign seas will continue with various swell directions 
from the west, south, and east.
